method: Static source/control-flow review, archive inspection, cleave facts (including available decoded strings), reproducible atomscan comparisons, upstream byte comparison and positive/near-miss controls. No specimen executed or installed.

evidence: The multipart POST puts <?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?> inside the upload filename. PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS causes filename data to be recorded in session state on a suitably configured target.

The query requests /tmp/sess_audit, pairs it with PHPSESSID=audit, and supplies cmd=whoami. A vulnerable file inclusion endpoint can evaluate the poisoned session and execute a request-controlled shell command.

This is a concrete exploit/request-fed webshell payload. localhost, audit identifiers and whoami are consistent with a proof of concept; no authorized deployment context is supplied. The verdict concerns the attack payload, not evidence that a machine was compromised.

All five hostile and seven suspicious findings are supported. They cover command execution, upload-progress code injection, and attempted session inclusion; no additional distinct hostile effect is present.

marker.contents: PHP session exploit: command webshell planted for session inclusion

evidence: The 573-byte archive contains only Cargo.toml, token.rs and crypto.rs. The source bytes match the pre-existing synthetic source-package fixture generator in testdata/triage/hopper-review-20261023/check.py.

Cargo.toml names review-library 1.0.0 and disables a build script. There is no src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, import/FFI definitions or caller; the functions use unresolved identifiers and are not a buildable Cargo program.

The worker makes call-shaped references to OpenProcessToken, DuplicateToken, ImpersonateLoggedOnUser and RtlAdjustPrivilege. The LSASS/Winlogon array is unused. No process enumeration, process-name comparison or link from a selected process to the token exists.

The crypto fragment declares APPB, v20 and app_bound_encrypted_key, plus DPAPI/CNG decryption calls. It neither reads a browser store nor passes a retrieved browser key to those calls; it has no output, network transfer, destruction, persistence or hidden stage.

The evidence favors an inert test fixture. Retain all API capabilities and suspicious archive-level crypto/token co-occurrence, but require actual process-enumeration/comparison evidence for the SYSTEM-token objective.

marker.contents: Rust review fixture: inert API fragments; fix escalation inference

sample_reports.identification: WSO2 Carbon Kernel 4.9.12 Go module source ZIP
evidence: SHA-256 e5681e2e233e387503ebba00e460266456a6cae3baa108a9f7a40d89f228df9c exactly matches the Go module proxy archive fetched with forager. This establishes byte agreement with upstream distribution, not a generic trust exception.
The project is WSO2 Carbon Kernel 4.9.12, a Java/OSGi server framework with administrative UI, registry/user management, clustering, crypto and deployment tools.

The classifier-driving admin/index.jsp tests the authenticated session and registered server-admin component, validates the session via a local AJAX endpoint, and loads local system-status HTML. skipLoginPage redirects to the existing login action, not an operator shell.

wso2server.sh prepares Java/classpaths, clears its temporary directory and starts org.wso2.carbon.bootstrap.Bootstrap. Main.writePID executes sh -c echo $PPID to record the PID. carbondump.bat gathers diagnostic network/system output; its accurate reconnaissance observation is retained.

EditArea is an editor bundle: eval dispatches editor callbacks and frame commands; unescape normalizes its script URL. The gzip member decompresses byte-for-byte to the plain JavaScript. The PHP compressor selects fixed editor asset/cache filenames, reads scripts, transforms source and emits/caches gzip; its regex-evaluation and filesystem traits remain.

Generic getChild/getChildCount, createGroup, addService, getString and stream-accessor syntax lack Android receiver identities. Prototype dataavailable is a generic custom DOM event; YUI CACHE_DATA is an identifier, not a disk path. The OTP rule crossed a closed input tag and matched otP in ForgotPassword.

The Eclipse processing instruction identifies its plugin descriptor. jQuery UI datepicker identifies jQuery UI, not the LocalCDN extension. Corrected these properties and preserved generic observations in accurate neutral categories.

Behavior and provenance favor legitimate upstream server code. No unauthorized collection, external secret transfer or covert command surface was found in the reviewed paths. Deployment authorization and target configuration are not supplied.

marker.contents: WSO2 Carbon 4.9.12: upstream server code; correct API and UI labels

Require a parsed LSASS/Winlogon equality comparison, parsed process enumeration, token-open reference, token duplication call and impersonation reference. The original chromium-crypto 0.5.3 positive retains this detection.

dependency_isolation.reason: The initial reference-following WSO2 scan fetched this package; its isolated before/after scans have identical trait sets and zero hostile/suspicious findings. The corrected LocalCDN marker came from the archive own older jQuery UI asset.

remaining_disagreements: The current model still flags WSO2 HOSTILE because of admin/index.jsp despite supported source/provenance evidence of a legitimate admin page. Its root probability 0.74479413 and level 0 are unchanged. No package exception or duplicate hostile rule was added to manipulate the classifier.
limits: HTTP success requires a vulnerable file-include endpoint and PHP upload-progress/session configuration; no server or runtime success was observed.
Static source cannot establish real-world deployment authorization. Rust fragments do not establish higher-authority token provenance or browser-key extraction.
WSO2 review covers the original archive and relevant execution paths; no compilation/runtime test or blanket assertion about every possible deployment vulnerability is made.
The scanner reports an older v18 model fact specification while the engine expects v21; this is a model compatibility limitation.
Initial scans followed references; before/after counts above use matching follow=none scans. Initial scans and logs remain in scratch for audit.
